verdict.rationale: Slate is a conversational coding agent. Its docs show users driving it with plain-English prompts, such as asking it to review the codebase architecture and write an ARCH.md. They also show users continuing to talk with it to plan, queue tasks and spin up agents, and steering it mid-run with messages. Community critique targets output quality, not whether natural-language operation works. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of natural-language control, and documentation of how reliably free-form commands map to actions such as config or workspace operations versus slash commands.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Please review the architecture of my entire codebase creating an ARCH.md and then give me ways I can improve it.
you can keep talking with Slate: plan next steps, queue up additional tasks, or spin up more agents to parallelize work across several tasks at once.
